edits.old: - **Skill identity/application invariant:** entries under authored `skillLibrary[personaId]` are Persona application profiles, not independent canonical Skill records. `content/library-model.js` collapses a shared Skill name to one stable Skill ID in `skillCatalog` while preserving every Persona profile separately. Shared operating/quality guidance remains keyed by that stable Skill ID. A repeated Skill name is therefore not evidence that the profile's definition, triggers, workflows, actions, or evidence are duplicate text. The #228 consolidation audit found 14 repeated Skill names: lifecycle status was shared across each family, but almost all application fields differed by Persona; introducing a second authored `skillCore` layer would add schema/maintenance cost without removing meaningful duplication. Factor application text into a portable core only when evidence shows the semantics themselves are shared, not merely the label.
edits.new: - **Skill identity/application invariant:** `skillCatalog` remains the single derived catalog of stable Skill identities. Its authored methods belong to the existing `skillLibrary` collection and source modules; distinct task conditions, instructions, workflow reach and evidence must remain separately inspectable. The accepted [CW-92 pilot source contract](docs/internal/cw92-capability-migration.md) permits neutral `skill-*` entries containing concrete, task-conditioned methods in `content/library-data/skills-core.js`, alongside unmigrated legacy arrays. Nested `method-*` IDs distinguish procedures, not professional profiles or actors. Persona metadata cannot determine method discovery or shared guidance. Legacy source associations are structured migration provenance and one-way derived compatibility, never selection authority or a second authored copy. Shared operating/quality guidance remains in its existing owner; repeated names alone do not justify merging methods. This accepted pilot contract defines the implementation target; source migration and consumer retirement require their own preservation and acceptance evidence, and nonpilot data is not implicitly migrated.
